q.s: Which Rigvedic assembly is mentioned the largest number of times (about 122 times) in the Rigveda?
q.x: The Vidatha is mentioned about 122 times, the most of any assembly, and was the first to disappear; the Sabha is mentioned 8 times.

q.s: In the Rigvedic period, women members of the Sabha were called:
q.x: Women who attended the Sabha were called Sabhavati.

q.s: The Amaravati School of art is noted for the use of which material?
q.x: Amaravati sculptures are in white limestone (marble-like); red sandstone is typical of Mathura and grey schist of Gandhara.

q.s: The Amaravati stupa was first identified in 1797 by:
q.x: Colin Mackenzie identified the stupa in 1797; Fergusson later called it the 'Epitome of Indian Architecture'.

q.s: The Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur was built by which Pala ruler?
q.x: Dharmapala built Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur (and founded Vikramashila); Gopala founded Odantapuri.

q.s: The Buddhist mahavihara of Odantapuri was founded by the Pala ruler:
q.x: Gopala founded Odantapuri; Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and built Somapura.

q.s: The Jain basadi at Vaddamanu in Guntur district is traditionally attributed to:
q.x: Vaddamanu basadi is ascribed to Samprati, Ashoka's grandson, a patron of Jainism.

q.s: Mahavira attained Kaivalya at the age of 42 at:
q.x: He attained Kaivalya under a sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama on the bank of the Rijupalika; he died at Pavapuri at 72.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mahavira is NOT correct?
q.x: He attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhikagrama on the Rijupalika; Sarnath is linked with the Buddha's first sermon.

q.s: According to the Arthashastra, the collector-general of revenue was called:
q.x: The Samaharta collected revenue; the Sannidhata kept the treasury and the Antapala guarded frontier forts.

q.s: With reference to Kautilya's Arthashastra, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Antapala was the commander of the army
The Karmantika was in charge of factories and mines
The Dandapala kept the royal treasury
q.x: The Karmantika handled factories and mines; the Samaharta collected revenue, the Sannidhata kept the treasury and the Antapala guarded the frontier.

q.s: Which of the following Ashokan edict sites is NOT located in Karnataka?
q.x: Erragudi is in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh; Maski (Raichur) and Brahmagiri and Siddapura (Chitradurga) are in Karnataka.

q.s: The gold coins of Chandragupta I bearing the legend 'Lichchhavayah' commemorate his marriage with:
q.x: The king-queen coins show Chandragupta I with his Lichchhavi queen Kumaradevi.

q.s: Which of the following works of Kalidasa is NOT a drama?
q.x: Ritusamhara is a lyrical poem on the seasons; the other three are his dramas.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of work and author is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Hitopadesha is by Narayana Pandita; the other pairs are correct.

q.s: The Harsha era began in the year:
q.x: Harsha acceded in 606 CE, starting the Harsha era; he died in 647 CE.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the court of Harshavardhana?
q.x: Vakpatiraja was the court poet of Yashovarman of Kannauj; the others adorned Harsha's court.

q.s: Harsha's Maha Moksha Parishad, held once in five years, met at:
q.x: The Maha Moksha Parishad met at Prayag every five years; Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth one. The Kannauj assembly was a separate religious assembly.

q.s: About the assemblies of Harshavardhana, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Maha Moksha Parishad met at Kannauj
The Prayag assembly was held every ten years
Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth Prayag assembly
q.x: Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth Prayag assembly; it met every five years and the Kannauj assembly lasted 23 days.

q.s: Under the Cholas, the assembly of Brahmins in brahmadeya villages was known as:
q.x: The Sabha or Mahasabha was the assembly of brahmadeya villages; the Ur was of non-brahmadeya villages and the Nagaram of merchants.

q.s: Under the Cholas, which of the following was NOT a local assembly?
q.x: The Samiti was a Rigvedic assembly; Ur, Sabha and Nagaram were Chola assemblies.

q.s: When Malik Kafur attacked Warangal in 1309-10, the Kakatiya ruler was:
q.x: Prataparudra II ruled Warangal; Ramachandra was the Yadava ruler of Devagiri.

q.s: Under Alauddin Khalji's market regulations, the superintendent of each market was called:
q.x: The Shahna-i-Mandi superintended each market; the Diwan-i-Riyasat ran the whole market system and Munhiyans were secret spies.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a part of Alauddin Khalji's market control machinery?
q.x: Diwan-i-Arz was the military department; the others ran the markets.

q.s: The 'blood and iron' policy is associated with which Delhi Sultan?
q.x: Balban followed the policy of blood and iron and the theory of divine kingship.

q.s: In the Kakatiya kingdom, the royal bodyguards were known as:
q.x: The Kakatiya royal bodyguards were the Lenkas.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Hadikat-us-Salatin was written by Ali bin Tahir Bustani on the Qutb Shahis.

q.s: The Chand Minar, built in 1435 by the Bahmanis, is located at:
q.x: Chand Minar stands at Daulatabad; Jahaz Mahal is at Mandu.

q.s: Which of the following monuments is NOT located at Mandu?
q.x: Atala Masjid is at Jaunpur (Sharqi); the others are at Mandu.

q.s: Sher Shah fought the battle of Samel in 1544 against:
q.x: Sher Shah defeated Maldeo Rathore of Marwar at Samel in 1544.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement of Sher Shah?
o: Victory at the First Battle of Panipat
Capture of Raisen from Puran Mal
q.x: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was won by Babur; Sher Shah defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540).

q.s: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the provincial units were called:
q.x: Golconda's provinces were tarafs; the village accountant was the kulkarni and the pargana officer the desai.

q.s: In the Qutb Shahi administration of Golconda, the village accountant was called:
q.x: The kulkarni was the village accountant and the desai the pargana officer.

q.s: Which saint of Andhra is known for criticising caste distinctions in his popular Telugu verses?
q.x: Vemana's verses attacked caste and ritualism; Potuluri Veerabrahmam too criticised caste.

q.s: The Mahanubhava sect of Maharashtra was founded by:
q.x: Chakradhar Swami founded the Mahanubhava sect; Dadu founded the Dadupanth of Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its founder?
q.x: The Rishi movement of Kashmir was founded by Sheikh Nuruddin (Nund Rishi), inspired by Lal Ded.

q.s: Which Sufi saint equated Alakh Niranjan with Khuda in his Hindi verses?
q.x: Hamiduddin Nagori, a Chishti saint, equated Alakh Niranjan with Khuda.

q.s: Shivaji ceded several forts to the Mughals by the Treaty of Purandar (1665), concluded with:
q.x: Shivaji signed the Treaty of Purandar with Raja Jai Singh in 1665; he later recaptured most of the forts.

q.s: The French factory at Machilipatnam was established in 1669 by:
q.x: Marcara set it up with permission of Abdullah Qutb Shah.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a French settlement in India?
q.x: Tranquebar was a Danish settlement; Yanam (1723) was the French possession in Andhra.

q.s: Which Governor-General systematically applied the Doctrine of Lapse from 1848?
q.x: Dalhousie announced and first applied it in 1848 (Satara), though he did not originate it.

q.s: Who became the first Viceroy of India under the Government of India Act, 1858?
q.x: The 1858 Act gave the Governor-General the title of Viceroy; Canning was the first.

q.s: 'Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind' (Causes of the Indian Revolt) was written by:
q.x: Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it in 1859; S.N. Sen wrote 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven'.

q.s: Which of the following books on the Revolt of 1857 is NOT correctly matched with its author?
o: The First Indian War of Independence – V.D. Savarkar
q.x: 'The First Indian War of Independence 1857-1859' is the collection of Marx and Engels; Savarkar wrote 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'.

q.s: In the Second Carnatic War, the English supported which claimant to the Nawabship of the Carnatic?
q.x: The English backed Muhammad Ali, while the French backed Chanda Sahib.

q.s: Peshwa Baji Rao II accepted the Subsidiary Alliance by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Bassein was signed on 31 December 1802; Deogaon was with the Bhonsle.

q.s: Which of the following Maratha chiefs was the LAST to accept the Subsidiary Alliance?
q.x: Holkar accepted it last, in 1818; the Peshwa signed at Bassein in 1802.

q.s: The Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24 was led by:
q.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa (Manyam) rebellion in the Godavari agency.

q.s: The transfer of the capital of British India from Calcutta to Delhi was announced at the Delhi Durbar of:
q.x: It was announced on 12 December 1911, along with the annulment of the Partition of Bengal.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911?
o: Annulment of the Partition of Bengal
Transfer of the capital to Delhi
q.x: The Partition of Bengal was made in 1905 under Curzon; 1911 annulled it.

q.s: In the revenue history of Andhra, 'Moturpha' was a tax on:
q.x: Moturpha was a tax on professions, trades and looms; Peshcush was the tribute of the Circar zamindars.

q.s: Which of the following revenue terms of colonial Andhra is NOT correctly matched?
o: Peshcush – Tribute paid by Circar zamindars
Moturpha – Land under direct Company control
Haveli – Land under direct Company control
q.x: Moturpha was a tax on professions, trades and looms.

q.s: The first Famine Code in British India (1883) followed the recommendations of the commission headed by:
q.x: The Strachey Commission (1880) led to the Famine Code of 1883; the Company had no famine code earlier.

q.s: Which document is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'?
q.x: Wood's Despatch (1854) was the first comprehensive plan for education; it favoured vernaculars at school level and English for higher studies.

q.s: India's first census, in 1872, was held during the Viceroyalty of:
q.x: The 1872 census was under Mayo; the first synchronous census of 1881 came under Ripon.

q.s: About the reforms of Mayo and Ripon, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Mayo introduced the first synchronous census of 1881
The first census of 1872 was held under Ripon
Ripon's Resolution of 1882 provided for local boards with a non-official majority
q.x: Ripon's 1882 Resolution is the Magna Carta of local self-government; the 1872 census was under Mayo.

q.s: The Sri Bagh Pact of 16 November 1937 was signed at the residence of:
q.x: It was concluded at Sri Bagh, the Madras house of Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao.

q.s: The All India Adi Hindu Conference was held at Lucknow in the year:
q.x: It was held at Lucknow in 1930; 1921 was the year of the first Adi-Andhra Sadassu at Amalapuram.

q.s: In the Andhra region, the social base of the Justice Party lay mainly among:
o: Intermediate landed castes like Reddys, Kammas and Kapus
q.x: The non-Brahmin movement in Andhra drew on intermediate landed castes such as Reddys, Kammas and Kapus.

q.s: The first Arya Samaj was established on 10 April 1875 at:
q.x: Dayananda founded the first Arya Samaj at Bombay; its headquarters later moved to Lahore and Punjab became its stronghold.

q.s: The Namdhari (Kuka) sect was founded in 1857 at Bhaini (Ludhiana) by:
q.x: Baba Ram Singh founded the Namdhari sect at Bhaini; he was deported to Rangoon after the Malerkotla clash of 1872.

q.s: The Ilbert Bill controversy took place during the Viceroyalty of:
q.x: The Bill, drafted by Law Member Courtenay Ilbert in Ripon's government, was passed in a diluted form on 25 January 1884.

q.s: The Indian Society of Oriental Art (1907) was founded by:
q.x: The Tagore brothers founded it; Nandalal Bose was Abanindranath's pupil.

q.s: Nandalal Bose, a pioneer of the Bengal School, was a pupil of:
q.x: Nandalal Bose trained under Abanindranath Tagore.

q.s: Who called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
q.x: Valentine Chirol, in 'Indian Unrest' (1910), called Tilak the Father of Indian Unrest.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a founder of the Deccan Education Society (1884)?
q.x: Tilak, Agarkar and Chiplunkar founded it; Gokhale joined later as a life member.

q.s: The arrest of Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Ghosh in 1908 led to which famous trial?
q.x: After the Muzaffarpur bomb (April 1908) the Anushilan group was rounded up and tried in the Alipore case.

q.s: In 1920 Gandhi became President of the All India Home Rule League and renamed it as:
q.x: Gandhi renamed it the Swarajya Sabha; Tilak's league (April 1916) preceded Besant's (September 1916).

q.s: Which woman revolutionary of the Chittagong group took cyanide after leading the attack on the Pahartali European Club in 1932?
q.x: Pritilata Waddedar took cyanide; Kalpana Dutt was transported for life and Bina Das fired at the Bengal Governor.

q.s: The Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League was adopted in the year:
q.x: Adopted in March 1940, it demanded independent states for Muslim-majority areas; the League first observed Pakistan Day on 23 March 1943.

q.s: About the Lahore Resolution of 1940, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The League first observed Pakistan Day on 23 March 1943
Rajagopalachari answered it with the Dravidistan demand
The word 'Pakistan' was used in it
It was moved at the Karachi session
q.x: Pakistan Day was first observed in 1943; the word 'Pakistan' was not in the resolution and Dravidistan was Periyar's demand.

q.s: The Cripps Mission came to India in the year:
q.x: Cripps came in March 1942; the League rejected it as it was based on a single Indian Union, and the Congress also rejected it.

q.s: The Royal Indian Navy mutiny of February 1946 began on board:
q.x: It began on HMIS Talwar in Bombay on 18 February 1946.

q.s: The book 'Guilty Men of India's Partition' was written by:
q.x: Lohia wrote it; 'India Divided' is by Rajendra Prasad and 'The Man Who Divided India' by Rafiq Zakaria.

q.s: Lord Mountbatten came to India as Viceroy in March 1947 succeeding:
q.x: Mountbatten succeeded Lord Wavell, after Attlee's declaration of 20 February 1947 fixed June 1948 as the deadline.

q.s: At the Tripuri Congress election of 1939, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated:
q.x: Bose defeated Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya; Gandhi called it 'my own defeat'.

q.s: Gandhi's view on property is best expressed by the concept of:
q.x: Gandhism stands for trusteeship; Marxism for abolition of private property.

q.s: Regarding Gandhian thought, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Gandhi called the State 'the march of God on earth'
Gandhi described the State as violence in a concentrated form
Gandhism stands for abolition of private property
q.x: Gandhi called the State violence in concentrated form; 'march of God on earth' is Hegel's phrase.

q.s: During the Quit India Movement in August 1942, the railway station and the Madras-Puri passenger train were burnt at:
q.x: Protesters burnt Tenali station and the train on 12 August 1942; the Bhimavaram Collectorate was attacked after firing on 17 August.

q.s: Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule by 'Operation Vijay' in the year:
q.x: Operation Vijay (18-19 December 1961) freed Goa, Daman and Diu; Dadra and Nagar Haveli were freed by volunteers in 1954.

q.s: The second Andhra Mahasabha, held at Vijayawada in 1914, was presided over by:
q.x: Nyapati Subba Rao presided at Vijayawada in 1914; the Raja of Panagal at Visakhapatnam in 1915.

q.s: The Dar Commission (1948) was appointed to examine the reorganisation of states on the basis of:
q.x: The Linguistic Provinces Commission under S.K. Dar examined linguistic provinces such as Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra, and favoured administrative convenience instead.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission suggested that Telangana could be unified with Andhra after the general elections of 1961 if supported by:
o: A simple majority of the Andhra Assembly
q.x: Para 386 of the SRC report required support of two-thirds of the elected members of the Telangana Assembly.

q.s: The megalithic burials of Andhra Pradesh, popularly called 'Rakshasa Gullu', belong to:
q.x: The megaliths belong to the Iron Age; dolmens were elite burials while commoners were buried in pits.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the megaliths of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: They belong to the Iron Age
They belong to the Old Stone Age
q.x: The megaliths are Iron Age burials, not Palaeolithic.

q.s: The Serivanija Jataka places 'Andhapura' on the banks of the river:
q.x: The Serivanija Jataka mentions Andhapura on the Telavaha.

q.s: The term 'Andhapatha' occurs in which Buddhist text?
q.x: 'Andhapatha' is mentioned in the Vinayavatthu.

q.s: Which metal was most commonly used for the coins of the Satavahanas?
q.x: Lead (potin also) was the most common Satavahana coin metal; bull-and-lion lead and copper coins are Pallava.

q.s: The Prakrit anthology 'Gathasaptasati' was compiled by the Satavahana king:
q.x: Hala, the 17th Satavahana king, compiled the Gathasaptasati.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of the Gathasaptasati?
o: It opens with a prayer to Shiva
It was written in Sanskrit by Kalidasa
q.x: It is a Prakrit anthology compiled by Hala.

q.s: The sculptors of the Amaravati School were known as:
q.x: The Amaravati sculptors were called Selavardhakulu; the Buddha is believed to have taught the Kalachakra at Dhanyakataka.

q.s: About Buddhism in Andhra, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Sanchi is part of the Andhra Pradesh Buddhist circuit
The Amaravati sculptors were called Sthapatis
The Buddha is believed to have first taught the Kalachakra at Dhanyakataka
q.x: Tradition places the first Kalachakra teaching at Dhanyakataka (Amaravati); Bavikonda and Thotlakonda are near Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Most of the donative inscriptions of the Ikshvakus at Nagarjunakonda are in:
q.x: They are mostly Prakrit records; the Ikshvakus were the first to date records by year, month and day.

q.s: The famous marble statue 'Veiled Rebecca' is displayed in:
q.x: Veiled Rebecca (Rome, 1876) is in the Salar Jung Museum, Hyderabad; the Bapu Museum at Vijayawada was the Victoria Jubilee Museum.

q.s: The Salar Jung Museum in Hyderabad was opened in the year:
q.x: It was opened in 1951 by Jawaharlal Nehru.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Salar Jung Museum?
q.x: It is in Hyderabad; the Bapu Museum is in Vijayawada.

q.s: The first capital of the Eastern Chalukyas under Kubja Vishnuvardhana was:
q.x: Pishtapura (Pithapuram) was the first capital; Vengi and then Rajamahendravaram followed.

q.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler shifted the capital to Rajamahendravaram?
q.x: Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram the capital; Jayasimha I had moved it to Vengi.

q.s: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple is the model of which temple style?
q.x: Draksharama is the model of the Eastern Chalukya or Chalukya-Chola style.

q.s: Ksheerarama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
q.x: Ksheerarama is at Palakollu (West Godavari); Kumararama is at Samalkot.

q.s: The Navabrahma temples at Alampur were built by:
q.x: The nine Navabrahma temples at Alampur are Badami Chalukya works.

q.s: Eastern Chalukya (Vengi School) temple building was concentrated mainly in:
q.x: Vengi School temples are mostly in the Krishna-Godavari delta.

q.s: 'Manucharitra', one of the Prabandhas of the Vijayanagara period, was written by:
q.x: Peddana, Andhra Kavitapitamaha, wrote Manucharitra; Nandi Timmana wrote Parijatapaharanam.

q.s: Which of the following works is NOT correctly matched with its author?
q.x: Varadambika Parinayam (Sanskrit) was written by Tirumalamba.

q.s: Nannaya borrowed the 'Akkara' metre from which language?
q.x: The Akkara metre came from Kannada; Nannaya also pioneered the Champu style.

q.s: The Salankayana dynasty of Vengi was founded by:
q.x: Vijaya Deva Varma founded the Salankayana line; Shantamula I founded the Ikshvaku line.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (founder – dynasty)?
q.x: Pulakesi I founded the Chalukya power of Badami, not the Pallavas.

q.s: In 1323 the Kakatiya kingdom was brought to an end by:
q.x: Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughlaq) captured Prataparudra in 1323.

q.s: Marco Polo, who praised the just rule of the Kakatiya queen Rudramadevi, landed at the port of:
q.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli and praised Rudramadevi; he also described diamond mines in the region.

q.s: About Marco Polo's account of the Kakatiya kingdom, which of the following statements is correct?
o: He said wheat was the only grain grown
He described the diamond mines of the region
He said Motupalli merchants were heavily taxed
q.x: He described the diamond mines and praised Rudramadevi's just rule; he said rice was the only grain.

q.s: After the fall of Warangal in 1323, the Tughlaqs placed Andhra under:
q.x: Andhra was placed under Malik Burhanuddin, with Malik Maqbul at Warangal; Zafar Khan founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.

q.s: In the Kakatiya administration, the officer in charge of collecting tolls and customs was the:
q.x: The Sunkadhikari collected tolls and customs; the Pradvivaka was a judicial adviser.

q.s: Which of the following Kakatiya officials is NOT correctly matched with the role?
q.x: The Ashtadasa Tirthas were the eighteen high officers of state.

q.s: Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta in a literary contest and received the Kanakabhishekam at the court of:
q.x: Srinatha, Kavi Sarvabhauma, won the Kanakabhishekam at Deva Raya II's court; he later joined Veerabhadra Reddi at Rajahmundry.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true about Srinatha?
o: He received Kanakabhishekam at Deva Raya II's court
He bore the title Kavi Sarvabhauma
He joined Veerabhadra Reddi's court at Rajahmundry
q.x: Manucharitra was written by Allasani Peddana.

q.s: Hoshang Shah of Malwa shifted his capital from Dhar to:
q.x: Hoshang Shah moved the capital to Mandu, home of the Hindola Mahal and Jahaz Mahal.

q.s: The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital are found at Hampi on the banks of the river:
q.x: Hampi lies on the Tungabhadra among granite hills that made a natural fortress; the site was inland, not coastal.

q.s: The Palnadu war of 1182 CE was fought at:
q.x: The war was fought at Karempudi; Srinatha's Palnati Veera Charitra narrates it.

q.s: The Telugu work 'Palnati Veera Charitra' was written by:
q.x: Srinatha wrote Palnati Veera Charitra on the Palnadu war.

q.s: The confederacy of Nayakas that liberated Andhra from Tughlaq rule after 1323 was led by:
q.x: Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka led the liberation, with Rekapalli as headquarters; the Kaluvacheru grant of Reddi queen Anitalli names the Nayakas.

q.s: About the liberation of Andhra after 1323, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It was led by Koppula Prolaya Nayaka
The Kaluvacheru grant was issued by a Musunuri queen
q.x: Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka led it from Rekapalli; the Kaluvacheru grant was issued by Reddi queen Anitalli.

q.s: The Pasupata sect, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by:
q.x: Lakulisa founded the Pasupata sect; Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya led the Aradhya Shaivas.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Shaiva sect?
q.x: Mahanubhava is a Krishna-centred sect of Maharashtra; the others are Shaiva.

q.s: Ptolemy referred to which Satavahana-age port of Andhra as 'Kantakossyla'?
q.x: Kantakossyla is Ghantasala; Ghantasala and Koddura were ports of Indo-Roman trade.

q.s: The Battle of Padmanabham (1794) was fought between the East India Company and:
q.x: Vijayarama Raju II of Vizianagaram was killed at Padmanabham in 1794.

q.s: The Gulugonda revolt (1845-48) in the Visakhapatnam agency was led by:
q.x: Chinna Bhupathi led the Gulugonda revolt with Korra Mallayya; Tamman Dora led the Rampa rising of 1879.

q.s: Which of the following agency risings of Andhra is NOT correctly matched with its leader?
q.x: The Manyam rebellion was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju; Komaram Bheem fought the Nizam in Adilabad.

q.s: In which year were the Godavari and Krishna districts formed by reorganising Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam districts?
q.x: The Godavari and Krishna districts were formed in 1859.

q.s: At the AICC meeting at Vijayawada in 1921, Gandhi's speech was translated into Telugu by:
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated Gandhi's speech at the AICC meeting of 31 March - 1 April 1921.

q.s: Which of the following leaders did NOT attend the AICC meeting at Vijayawada in 1921?
q.x: Gandhi, Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das and the Ali brothers attended; Jinnah had distanced himself from Non-Cooperation.

q.s: The Chirala-Perala movement of 1921 was led by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led it; the people moved to a camp called Ramnagar and the volunteer corps was the Ramadandu.

q.s: The volunteer corps of the Chirala-Perala movement (1921) was called the:
q.x: Duggirala's Ramadandu was the corps; the Shanti Sena belonged to Pedanandipadu.

q.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted by Parliament in the year:
q.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act dates from 1961; the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act is of 1988.

q.s: Who wrote the Telugu poem 'Gabbilam', in which a bat carries the message of an untouchable?
q.x: Gurram Jashuva's Gabbilam uses the bat, shut out of the temple, as the symbol of the untouchable.

q.s: Chanda Pradyota, a contemporary of the Buddha, was the ruler of:
q.x: Chanda Pradyota ruled Avanti; Prasenajit ruled Kosala and Udayana Vatsa.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT a ruler contemporary of the Buddha?
q.x: Chandragupta Maurya came about two centuries after the Buddha.

q.s: Who was left by Muhammad Ghori as his representative in India and later became the first Sultan of Delhi?
q.x: Aibak represented Ghori after 1192 and became the first Sultan in 1206.

q.s: Irawati Karve's 'Kinship Organization in India' (1953) divided India into four kinship zones. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
q.x: Karve's zones were North, Central, South and East.

q.s: In the caste system, castes are ranked mainly on the basis of the principle of:
q.x: Ranking rests on ritual purity and pollution; varna is the four-fold order and jati the real local birth groups.

q.s: The Haryana State Employment of Local Candidates Act, 2020, providing local job quotas, was struck down in November 2023 by:
o: The Punjab and Haryana High Court
q.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court held it contrary to Articles 14, 15, 16 and 19.

q.s: The NSCN split into NSCN-IM and NSCN-K in the year:
q.x: Formed in 1980 after rejecting the Shillong Accord, the NSCN split in 1988; its Greater Nagaland demand is secessionist.

q.s: The 'Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report', which ranks countries in tiers, is published by:
q.x: The US State Department publishes the TIP Report; UNODC publishes the Global Report on Trafficking in Persons.

q.s: 'SHe-Box', an online portal, is meant for registering complaints of:
q.x: SHe-Box routes workplace sexual harassment complaints directly to the Internal or Local Committee under the POSH Act.

q.s: Under MGNREGA, at least what proportion of the beneficiaries must be women?
q.x: At least one-third of the workers must be women; 100 days of work per rural household is guaranteed.

q.s: Under MGNREGA, an unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within how many days of demand?
q.x: The allowance is due if work is not given within 15 days.

q.s: 'Sambal' and 'Samarthya' are the two sub-schemes of which umbrella mission of the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
q.x: Mission Shakti has Sambal (safety) and Samarthya (empowerment); Mission Vatsalya is for child protection.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of Mission Shakti?
q.x: Child protection comes under Mission Vatsalya; the others are under Sambal and Samarthya.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's 'Talliki Vandanam' scheme, the annual assistance per school-going child is:
q.x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per school-going child a year; Stree Shakti gives women free bus travel.

q.s: India granted Most Favoured Nation (MFN) status to Pakistan in the year:
q.x: India granted MFN status in 1996 and withdrew it in February 2019, raising duties on Pakistani goods to 200%.

q.s: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 between India and Pakistan was signed with the mediation of:
q.x: Soviet Premier Kosygin mediated; Lal Bahadur Shastri died at Tashkent soon after signing.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the eight baskets of the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue?
q.x: Nuclear disarmament was not a basket; the others, with J&K and terrorism, were.

q.s: India has developed an airstrip and jetty on Agalega island, which belongs to:
q.x: Agalega is part of Mauritius; Assumption Island belongs to Seychelles.

q.s: In 2016 the United States designated India as its:
q.x: India became a Major Defense Partner in 2016 and received STA-1 status in 2018.

q.s: In March 2025, India chaired which UN body dealing with drug control policy?
q.x: India chaired the Commission on Narcotic Drugs (CND), the policy body of the UN drug-control system.

q.s: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) was founded in 1950 by:
q.x: Maulana Azad, the first Education Minister, founded the ICCR.

q.s: About the Festivals of India, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The festivals were organised by UNESCO
The first Festival of India was held in the USA
The first Festival of India was held in the UK in 1982
The 1987-88 Festival of India was held in China
q.x: The first Festival of India was held in Britain in 1982; the 1987-88 festival was in the USSR.

q.s: 'The Resistance Front' (TRF), active in Jammu and Kashmir, is considered a proxy of:
q.x: TRF is a proxy of Lashkar-e-Taiba, which was founded in 1990 in Kunar, Afghanistan.

q.s: The People's War Group (PWG) was founded in 1980 by:
q.x: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the PWG in Andhra Pradesh; it merged into CPI (Maoist) in 2004.

q.s: Article 1 of the Constitution of India describes India as a:
q.x: Article 1 says 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'; the word 'federation' is not used.

q.s: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: An integrated judiciary is unitary; bicameralism and division of powers are federal features.

q.s: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was NOT borrowed from the USA?
q.x: The Concurrent List came from Australia; the other three are from the US Constitution.

q.s: In India's parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
q.x: Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

q.s: About forms of government, which of the following statements is correct?
o: India's Council of Ministers is responsible to the Rajya Sabha
The parliamentary form rests on separation of powers
The presidential form rests on co-operation between legislature and executive
The parliamentary form rests on co-operation and co-ordination between legislature and executive
q.x: The parliamentary form rests on co-operation between organs; the presidential form on separation of powers.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (feature – source) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Liberty, equality and fraternity came from France.

q.s: Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship by naturalisation is provided in:
q.x: Naturalisation is Section 6; descent is Section 4, registration Section 5 and incorporation of territory Section 7.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a mode of acquiring Indian citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
q.x: The Act provides birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory; marriage alone does not confer citizenship.

q.s: According to Census 2011, Hindus formed what percentage of India's population?
q.x: Hindus were 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3% and Sikhs 1.7%.

q.s: Up to 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in educational institutions is provided under:
q.x: Article 15(6), inserted by the 103rd Amendment (2019), enables EWS reservation; 15(3) covers women and children.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a right of an arrested person under Article 22(1) and 22(2)?
o: To be released on bail as of right
To be informed of the grounds of arrest
To consult a lawyer of his choice
To be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours
q.x: Article 22 does not guarantee bail as of right; the other three are guaranteed.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a proclamation of Emergency is subject to judicial review and strike down the extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles?
q.x: Minerva Mills (1980) struck down that part of the 42nd Amendment; Kesavananda struck down the second provision of Article 31C.

q.s: The 'doctrine of pleasure' regarding civil servants is contained in which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 310 embodies the doctrine of pleasure, subject to safeguards in Article 311.

q.s: About the Supreme Court and precedent, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Article 141 binds only High Courts and not subordinate courts
The Supreme Court is bound by its own earlier decisions
Article 141 makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts in India
Ram Jawaya Kapur held that India follows rigid separation of powers
q.x: Article 141 binds all courts in India, but not the Supreme Court itself.

q.s: The 'doctrine of eclipse' was laid down by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: Bhikaji Narain (1955) laid down eclipse; Basheshar Nath dealt with waiver and Balsara with pith and substance.

q.s: The doctrine of 'pith and substance' was applied by the Supreme Court in:
o: State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara
Bhikaji Narain v. State of MP
K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa
q.x: Balsara (1951) applied pith and substance; Gajapati Narayan Deo dealt with colourable legislation.

q.s: How many members does the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament have?
q.x: The PAC has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha); the Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Which of the following parliamentary committees has NO members from the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: All 30 members of the Estimates Committee are from the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Which parliamentary committee is described as a 'continuous economy committee'?
q.x: The Estimates Committee, first constituted in 1950 on John Mathai's suggestion, is the continuous economy committee.

q.s: The Committee on Public Undertakings (1964) was created on the recommendation of the:
q.x: COPU was set up on the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation.

q.s: While a resolution for the removal of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly is under consideration, the Speaker:
o: Does not preside but can vote in the first instance
Can vote only in case of a tie
q.x: Under Article 181 he does not preside, but may speak and vote in the first instance.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the number of Assembly seats allotted to residuary Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Section 17 gave AP 175 and Telangana 119 seats; Section 26 provides for raising them to 225 and 153.

q.s: An ordinance promulgated by the Governor ceases to operate, unless approved earlier, at the expiry of:
o: Six weeks from the reassembly of the legislature
q.x: Under Article 213 it lapses six weeks after the reassembly of the State Legislature.

q.s: About the Governor's ordinance-making power, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Every ordinance needs the President's approval
The Governor can withdraw an ordinance at any time
An ordinance lapses six months after promulgation
The Governor can issue ordinances when the legislature is in session
q.x: The Governor may withdraw an ordinance at any time; it lapses six weeks after reassembly.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment dropped Bihar from the States required to have a Minister in charge of tribal welfare?
q.x: The 94th Amendment (2006) replaced Bihar with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand; the 91st capped the size of Councils of Ministers.

q.s: Which of the following States is NOT required by Article 164(1) to have a Minister in charge of tribal welfare?
q.x: The provision now applies to Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.

q.s: Under the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, a Minister held in custody for how many consecutive days would be removed from office?
q.x: A PM, CM or Minister held in custody for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five years or more would be removed on the 31st day.

q.s: The first Lok Adalat camp in India was held in 1982 in the State of:
q.x: The first Lok Adalat camp was held in Gujarat in 1982.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that federalism is a basic feature and that a proclamation under Article 356 is open to judicial review?
o: State of West Bengal v. Union of India
q.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) made Article 356 justiciable.

q.s: The members of a Joint State Public Service Commission are appointed by:
o: The Governors of the States concerned
q.x: JSPSC members are appointed by the President; the JSPSC is created by an Act of Parliament on the request of the States.

q.s: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by:
q.x: Under Articles 243K and 243ZA, the State Election Commission, appointed by the Governor, conducts them.

q.s: About State-level bodies, which of the following statements is correct?
o: State Information Commissions are constitutional bodies
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor
Local body elections are conducted by the ECI
State Commissions for SCs are created by Article 338
q.x: The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner; SICs are statutory under the RTI Act.

q.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status by the:
q.x: The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B; the 89th Amendment split the NCSC and NCST.

q.s: About changes in the status of commissions, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Federal Public Service Commission was set up in 1950
The NCSC and NCST were split by the 89th Amendment, 2003
The 42nd Amendment created the joint National Commission for SCs and STs
The NCBC was made constitutional by the 103rd Amendment
q.x: The 89th Amendment split them; the joint commission came from the 65th Amendment and the NCBC from the 102nd.

q.s: Jains were notified as a national minority community in the year:
q.x: Jains were notified in 2014, joining Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis.

q.s: About the National Commission for Minorities, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It was set up as a constitutional body in 1978
Jains were notified as a minority in 2004
It was given statutory status by the NCM Act, 1992
q.x: The 1978 Commission was made statutory in 1992; it has seven members.

q.s: Under the Prakash Singh judgment (2006), the State Police Complaints Authority is to be headed by a:
q.x: The SPCA is headed by a retired High Court judge; the DGP is chosen from a UPSC panel of three.

q.s: About the Prakash Singh judgment (2006), which of the following statements is correct?
o: The State Police Complaints Authority is headed by a retired IAS officer
The Police Act, 1861 was repealed after it
The DGP is to be chosen from a UPSC panel and have a minimum two-year tenure
q.x: It issued seven directives; the DGP is selected from a UPSC panel; the 1861 Act is still in force.

q.s: The 'full faith and credit' clause in Article 261 of the Indian Constitution is modelled on the Constitution of:
q.x: It is modelled on the US Constitution; only final civil judgments are executable anywhere in India.

q.s: The National Education Policy 2020 sets a target of public spending on education at:
q.x: NEP 2020 targets 6% of GDP; the National Health Policy 2017 targets 2.5% of GDP for health.

q.s: The first general elections of India (1951-52) were conducted under the Chief Election Commissioner:
q.x: Sukumar Sen was the first CEC; simultaneous polls continued until 1967.

q.s: About simultaneous elections in India, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They were held in the first four general elections up to 1967
q.x: Lok Sabha and Assembly polls were held together in 1951-52, 1957, 1962 and 1967.

q.s: Under the 84th Amendment (2001), the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among States remains based on the census of:
q.x: Allocation stays frozen on the 1971 census until the first census after 2026; this freeze is at the heart of the delimitation debate.

q.s: Under the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1996, a candidate can contest a general election from a maximum of:
q.x: The 1996 Act capped contests at two seats and let a recognised party substitute a deceased candidate within 7 days.

q.s: Part IX of the Constitution, dealing with Panchayats, gives effect to which Directive Principle?
q.x: Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats; Part IX covers Articles 243 to 243O.

q.s: About Part IX of the Constitution, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It was added by the 74th Amendment
q.x: Part IX (73rd Amendment) covers Articles 243-243O; 243P-243ZG is Part IXA on Municipalities.

q.s: Under the Sixth Schedule, an Autonomous District Council consists of how many members?
q.x: A District Council has 30 members: 26 elected by adult franchise and 4 nominated by the Governor.

q.s: Under the Sixth Schedule, how many members of a District Council are nominated by the Governor?
q.x: Four of the 30 members are nominated by the Governor.

q.s: The 'Stand-Up India' scheme provides bank loans of what range to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs?
q.x: Stand-Up India loans range from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.

q.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1922-24 was mainly directed against:
q.x: The tribals resented forest laws that curbed podu (shifting) cultivation; Alluri Sitarama Raju led the revolt.

q.s: Who was the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog?
q.x: Arvind Panagariya was the first; full-time members hold Minister of State rank.

q.s: About NITI Aayog, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Its Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister
It is chaired by the Finance Minister
Its full-time members have Cabinet Minister rank
It is the nodal agency for GDP estimation
q.x: The PM chairs it and appoints the Vice-Chairperson; full-time members have MoS rank.

q.s: Which of the following statements about NITI Aayog is correct?
o: It was created by an Act of Parliament in 2015
It allocates plan funds to the States
It came into being on 1 January 2015 by a Union Cabinet resolution
It is a constitutional body under Article 280
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution and is neither constitutional nor statutory; it does not allocate funds.

q.s: The term 'Washington Consensus' was coined in 1989 by:
q.x: John Williamson coined it for a package of reforms including privatisation and deregulation.

q.s: Defence production in India was opened to the private sector in the year:
q.x: Defence was opened to private firms in 2001; disinvestment began in 1991-92.

q.s: The Offer for Sale (OFS) route for disinvestment through stock exchanges has been used since:
q.x: OFS has been used since 2012; in a minority stake sale the government retains at least 51%.

q.s: PM-WANI, the scheme for public Wi-Fi hotspots, is implemented by:
q.x: PM-WANI is run by the Department of Telecommunications; PMGDISHA is a MeitY digital literacy scheme.

q.s: CPGRAMS, the online grievance portal of the Government of India, was launched in 2007 by:
q.x: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances launched CPGRAMS.

q.s: CPGRAMS can be accessed through which of the following?
o: Web portal, mobile app and UMANG
q.x: CPGRAMS is available 24x7 on the web, an app and UMANG.

q.s: The institution of Ombudsman originated in:
q.x: It began in Sweden in 1809.

q.s: Which State was the first in India to set up a Lokayukta (1971)?
q.x: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971; the terms Lokpal and Lokayukta were coined by L.M. Singhvi.

q.s: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 seeks to replace the UGC, AICTE and:
q.x: It would repeal the UGC, AICTE and NCTE Acts; the National Medical Commission is not covered.

q.s: The NSG granted a waiver to India for civil nuclear trade in:
q.x: The NSG waiver came on 6 September 2008; the Hyde Act was of 2006 and the 123 Agreement was signed in October 2008.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the population of residual Andhra Pradesh was about:
q.x: Residual AP had about 4.96 crore people and kept the entire coastline.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's cultured-shrimp exports?
q.x: AP contributes about 75% of cultured-shrimp exports and about 29% of India's fish production.

q.s: The MSP-based procurement support of India is challenged at the WTO as falling in which category of subsidy?
q.x: MSP support is counted in the trade-distorting Amber Box against an outdated 1986-88 reference price.

q.s: Which State has the highest Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) value among the following?
q.x: Bihar's MPI value is about 0.16, the highest; Kerala's is 0.002.

q.s: India's first municipal bond was issued in 1997 by:
q.x: Bangalore Mahanagara Palike issued it in 1997; Ahmedabad issued the first without a State guarantee in 1998.

q.s: Indira Kranthi Patham (2004-05) in Andhra Pradesh was formed by merging DWCRA with:
q.x: IKP merged Velugu and DWCRA and is run by SERP, the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, how many Rajya Sabha seats were allotted to Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: AP got 11 Rajya Sabha seats (Telangana 7) and 25 Lok Sabha seats (Telangana 17).

q.s: The vision document 'Swarna Andhra @2047' was released by:
q.x: It is the AP government's vision for 2047; NITI Aayog has its own Viksit Bharat vision.

q.s: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, a GIS-based integrated infrastructure planning platform, was launched in:
q.x: It was launched in October 2021; the National Infrastructure Pipeline came earlier, in December 2019.

q.s: As per PLFS 2023-24 (usual status), India's unemployment rate was:
q.x: The all-India rate was 3.2%, with rural 2.5% and urban 5.1%.

q.s: The 'trickle-down' theory of development holds that:
o: Growth must be curbed to cut inequality
Benefits of growth reach the poor automatically
q.x: Trickle-down assumes benefits of growth percolate down automatically; the Gandhian model stresses decentralisation and village industry.

q.s: The book 'An Uncertain Glory: India and its Contradictions' (2013) was written by:
q.x: Sen and Dreze wrote it; 'Why Growth Matters' is by Bhagwati and Panagariya.

q.s: Within Andhra Pradesh, which region lags behind in agricultural productivity mainly because it is largely rain-fed?
q.x: Rain-fed Rayalaseema lags while the irrigated deltas gain.

q.s: As per the RBI's update of the Rangarajan poverty line using HCES 2022-23, which State had the highest rural poverty?
q.x: Chhattisgarh had the highest rural (25.1%) and urban poverty; Himachal Pradesh had the lowest rural poverty.

q.s: As per the National MPI, which State recorded the largest number of people (about 5.94 crore) escaping multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23?
q.x: Uttar Pradesh had the largest number exiting poverty; Bihar has the highest and Kerala the lowest MPI.

q.s: As per PLFS 2025, the unemployment rate among tertiary-educated youth aged 18-29 was about:
q.x: It was 29.4%, against 14.8% for all youth of that age; 40.1% is the NEET share of tertiary-educated youth.

q.s: National Statistics Day, observed on 29 June, marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: Statistics Day honours P.C. Mahalanobis, who chaired the National Income Committee (1949) that led to the NSS.

q.s: The Gadgil formula for the distribution of central plan assistance to States was first adopted in:
q.x: The Gadgil formula (1969) gave way to the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula in 1991.

q.s: Special Category States received central plan assistance in the ratio of:
q.x: Special Category States got 90% as grant and 10% as loan; others 30% grant and 70% loan.

q.s: During the 1991 balance of payments crisis, the RBI pledged about 47 tonnes of gold with:
o: The Bank of England and the Bank of Japan
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York
q.x: About 47 tonnes went to the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan; earlier about 20 tonnes were sold to UBS through SBI.

q.s: Under Special Category Status, the Centre-State funding ratio for centrally sponsored schemes is:
q.x: SCS carries a 90:10 funding pattern; a special package is project-linked.

q.s: Which of the following is a primary function of money?
q.x: Medium of exchange and measure of value are primary; store of value and deferred payments are secondary; basis of credit is contingent.

q.s: About the functions of money, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Measure of value is a primary function
Medium of exchange is a contingent function
Basis of credit is a secondary function
Store of value is a primary function
q.x: Medium of exchange and measure of value are primary functions.

q.s: The nodal department for the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is the:
q.x: PMJDY, launched on 28 August 2014, is run by the Department of Financial Services.

q.s: The Minimum Reserve System of note issue was adopted by the RBI in the year:
q.x: In 1956 it replaced the Proportional Reserve System, with a minimum reserve of ₹515 crore (₹400 crore foreign securities, ₹115 crore gold).

q.s: Under the flexible inflation-targeting framework, the RBI's inflation target band for CPI inflation is:
q.x: The target is 4% CPI inflation within 2-6%; failure means staying outside the band for three consecutive quarters.

q.s: About the flexible inflation-targeting framework, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Failure is deemed after inflation stays outside the band for three consecutive quarters
The failure clause has never been invoked
CPI-Combined is compiled by the RBI
Failure is deemed after inflation stays outside the band for three consecutive months
q.x: Failure is three consecutive quarters outside 2-6%; it was first invoked in 2022; CPI is compiled by the NSO.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the All-India Financial Institutions regulated by the RBI?
q.x: The RBI regulates EXIM Bank, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI and NaBFID; LIC is under IRDAI.

q.s: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, the adjudicating authority for the insolvency of companies and LLPs is the:
q.x: NCLT handles companies and LLPs; DRT handles individuals and partnership firms; NCLAT hears appeals.

q.s: The NCLAT hears appeals from all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Appeals against SEBI go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

q.s: Under the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) scheme, States receive:
q.x: SASCI gives States 50-year interest-free loans for capital investment.

q.s: The Oil Pool Account, along with the Administered Pricing Mechanism, was dismantled in the year:
q.x: It closed on 1 April 2002; under-recoveries were then met partly through oil bonds.

q.s: The 'three functions of the budget' (allocation, distribution and stabilisation) were given by:
q.x: Richard Musgrave set out the three functions; the N.K. Singh Committee proposed the 60% debt anchor.

q.s: Indirect taxes in India are administered by:
q.x: CBIC administers indirect taxes and CBDT direct taxes; indirect taxes are generally regressive.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a direct tax?
q.x: GST is an indirect tax administered under CBIC.

q.s: The GST Council is provided for under which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council constituted by the President; 269A deals with IGST.

q.s: Which Article inserted by the 101st Amendment provides for IGST on inter-State trade?
q.x: Article 269A provides for IGST, levied and collected by the Union.

q.s: GST compensation to States for 2017-22 was paid on the basis of an assured annual revenue growth of:
q.x: States were assured 14% annual growth over the 2015-16 base for five years.

q.s: The fiscal deficit target in the Union Budget Estimates 2026-27 is:
q.x: BE 2026-27 puts the fiscal deficit at 4.3% of GDP, below the 4.8% of 2024-25.

q.s: India's first Export Processing Zone was set up in 1965 at:
q.x: Kandla was the first EPZ; marine products are AP's top merchandise export.

q.s: Under Press Note 3 (2020), FDI from a country sharing a land border with India is allowed only through:
q.x: Press Note 3 requires prior government approval for such FDI; it covers neighbours like China and Bhutan.

q.s: As per Agriculture Census 2015-16, small and marginal holdings formed about what share of all operational holdings?
q.x: They formed 86.2% of holdings; Nagaland had the largest average holding.

q.s: How many of the four indicators of the Global Hunger Index concern children?
q.x: Child stunting, child wasting and under-five mortality concern children; undernourishment is the fourth.

q.s: Which State is the leading producer of soybean in India?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh leads in soybean; Rajasthan leads in rapeseed-mustard and Gujarat in cotton.

q.s: Which of the following crop-state pairs is NOT correctly matched (leading producer)?
q.x: Maharashtra leads in cashew, followed by Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (NMEO-OP), launched in August 2021, focuses especially on:
o: North-East and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
q.x: NMEO-OP (₹11,040 crore) focuses on the North-East and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; NMEO-Oilseeds (2024) covers primary oilseeds.

q.s: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) functions under the Ministry of:
q.x: KVIC is a statutory body under the KVI Act, 1956, working under the Ministry of MSME.

q.s: MSMEs contribute about what share of India's GDP?
q.x: MSMEs contribute about 31.1% of GDP.

q.s: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are being developed as Multi-Service Centres with the support of:
q.x: NABARD supports the conversion of PACS into Multi-Service Centres; AP ranks first in SHG-Bank Linkage.

q.s: 'Krishi UDAN' scheme is meant for:
o: Moving perishable farm produce by air
q.x: Krishi UDAN helps transport perishable agri-produce by air; the 2018-19 Budget proposed upgrading 22,000 rural haats into GrAMs.

q.s: About agricultural marketing reforms, which of the following statements is correct?
o: 22,000 APMC mandis were to be converted into GrAMs
22,000 rural haats were to be upgraded into Gramin Agricultural Markets
The Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund was only for APMCs
GrAMs were proposed in the 2010 Budget

q.s: The Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for Vegetables and Flowers in Andhra Pradesh is located at:

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a sub-scheme of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)?
o: Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States

q.s: The JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant in Kadapa district is to draw its water from:

q.s: Under AP's IT & GCC Policy 4.0 (2024-29), a 'Global Capability Centre' refers to:
o: A data centre owned by the State
A multinational company's own offshore unit

q.s: The Earth moves fastest in its orbit when it is at:

Its degree shrinks towards the poles
Its degree is about 55.5 km at 60°
Its degree is the same length everywhere

q.s: Which layer of the Earth accounts for the largest share (about 83%) of its volume?
q.x: The mantle makes up about 83% of volume; the core only about 16%.

q.s: A rotational slip of material along a curved surface in weak, saturated soil is called a:
q.x: A slump is a rotational slide; a rockfall is free fall from cliffs.

o: The Coriolis force is negligible there

q.s: The pre-monsoon thunderstorms along the coasts of Kerala and Karnataka are known as:

q.s: Which of the following local winds is NOT correctly matched?
o: Loo – Hot dry westerly of the Indo-Gangetic plain
Mango showers – Kerala and Karnataka coasts
Kaal Baisakhi – West Bengal and Assam
q.x: Aandhi are dust storms of north-west India.

q.s: The subtropical high-pressure belts are associated with:
o: Rising moist air and heavy rainfall
Sinking dry air and hot deserts
Meeting of westerlies and polar easterlies
q.x: Sinking dry air in the subtropical highs produces hot deserts; the subpolar low lies at about 60°-65°.

q.s: The Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), which influences active and break spells of the Indian monsoon, is a pulse of clouds and rain that moves:
q.x: The MJO moves eastward and recurs every 30-60 days.

q.x: The mesopause is at about 80 km; the stratopause is at about 50 km.

q.s: The highest peak of Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Jindhagada (1,690 m) is the highest, slightly above Arma Konda (1,680 m).

q.s: The Diviseema cyclone, which caused about 10,000 deaths in Andhra Pradesh, struck in the year:

q.x: Hudhud was named by Oman; it is the Arabic name of the hoopoe bird.

q.s: Contour bunding as a soil conservation method is most suitable for:
q.x: Contour bunds along contour lines slow runoff on slopes; they have no role on flat flood plains.

q.s: World Tsunami Awareness Day is observed every year on:

q.s: Which sector is the largest user of water in India?

q.s: About India's water resources, which of the following statements is correct?
o: India has about 4% of the world's renewable water resources
India receives about 1,869 bcm of rainfall a year
Industry is the largest user of water
Per-capita water availability has risen since Independence
q.x: India has about 4% of the world's water and 2.4% of its land; agriculture is the largest user.

q.s: The Bailadila iron-ore mines are located in which State?

q.s: Which of the following iron-ore areas is NOT correctly matched with its State?
q.x: Bailadila is in Dantewada, Chhattisgarh.

q.s: Which iron ore has the highest iron content?
q.x: Magnetite is the richest; haematite is the most widely used.

q.s: Which iron ore is the most widely used and forms India's largest reserve type?
q.x: Haematite is the most used; magnetite is the richest.

q.s: The Nellore mica belt of Andhra Pradesh belongs to which rock system?
q.x: Nellore mica schists and the Chittoor-Anantapur gold belt lie in Dharwar rocks.

q.s: Which of the following is the oldest rock system of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Archaean system is the oldest and contains no fossils.

q.s: NHPC, India's hydropower generation PSU, was set up in the year:

q.s: Wheat in India is mainly grown as a:

q.s: About wheat cultivation in India, which of the following statements is correct?

Wheat needs bright, warm sunshine at the time of ripening
Wheat is mainly a kharif crop

q.s: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) was set up under an Act passed in:
q.x: The APEDA Act dates from 1985.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana?
q.x: Soil Health Cards are a separate scheme; SAMPADA covers food parks, cold chain and processing clusters.

q.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at which Ministerial Conference?
q.x: It was adopted at MC12, Geneva, in 2022.

q.s: Which of the following sugar industry by-products is NOT correctly matched with its use?
o: Bagasse – Boiler fuel and paper pulp
q.x: Molasses is used for alcohol and ethanol; paper pulp comes from bagasse.

q.s: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane is fixed by:
q.x: FRP is fixed by the Centre; some States announce a State Advised Price (SAP).

q.s: Which is the only major port of Andhra Pradesh?

q.x: Vadhavan is in Palghar district.

q.s: Puttaparthi in Andhra Pradesh has a private airstrip owned by:
q.x: The airstrip belongs to the Sri Sathya Sai Trust and is not one of AP's six operational airports.

q.s: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) was built mainly to decongest:
q.x: JNPT (1989) was a satellite port for Mumbai; it is India's largest container port.

q.s: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (Dadri to JNPT) is funded mainly by:
q.x: JICA funds the Western DFC; the World Bank funds the Eastern DFC.

q.x: The World Bank funds the Eastern DFC; JICA funds the Western DFC.

q.s: The LEADS (Logistics Ease Across Different States) index is brought out by:
q.x: DPIIT has issued LEADS since 2018; it ranks Indian States and UTs.

q.x: China has about 48,000 km of high-speed rail; India's network is the fourth longest overall.

q.x: West Godavari had the highest share of agricultural labourers; Chittoor had the highest share of cultivators.

q.x: Kotias live in the Visakhapatnam highlands; the Chenchus are the Nallamala tribe.

q.x: QCI conducts the survey, which began in 2016 with 73 cities.

q.x: Sathyamangalam is in Tamil Nadu.

PaaS provides a platform to build and run applications
SaaS gives only raw computing power
